name: MathVista
description: MathVista is a benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks. It consists of 6,141 examples, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). Completing these tasks requires fine-grained, deep visual understanding and compositional reasoning.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
publisher: UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research
citeAs: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao. MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. ICLR 2024.
rai:dataCollection: MathVista was collected from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA). For existing MathQA datasets, 9 datasets were collected including 4 for GPS, 2 for MWP, and 2 for TQA, limited to 400 examples each. For VQA datasets, 19 datasets were reviewed and examples likely involving mathematical reasoning were automatically selected using heuristic rules (numeric answers or quantity words), yielding 4,949 examples. Three expert annotators manually labeled these to determine mathematical reasoning involvement, resulting in 2,739 examples after majority voting and limiting each source to 400 examples.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data was sourced from 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets) and 3 newly created datasets. MathQA datasets include geometry problem solving, math word problems with visual contexts, and textbook question answering. VQA datasets were reviewed from over 70 candidates, selecting those containing math-related instances. New datasets include IQTest (228 examples from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms), FunctionQA (400 examples emphasizing functional plots and algebraic reasoning), and PaperQA (107 examples from academic papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface).
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA examples were sourced from papers released in August 2023. The overall collection process timeframe is not explicitly stated.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely involving mathematical reasoning (examples with numeric answers or quantity words). Each source dataset was limited to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. A two-step quality check process was employed: initial independent annotation by three reviewers with 99.2% inter-annotation consistency, followed by team discussion to resolve the 6 disagreements among 736 newly collected questions.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: All questions in the three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process. A two-step annotation process was used: three reviewers independently annotated each dataset, achieving 99.2% inter-annotation consistency rate. Discrepancies (6 out of 736 questions) were resolved through discussion among the entire review team. Examples are annotated with metadata including question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, and visual context. Mathematical reasoning categories were automatically annotated and verified by expert annotators manually labeling 1,000 examples, showing 94.1% exact match and 98.79% individual label accuracy.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A custom GUI annotation tool was developed for the annotation process, as illustrated in the paper.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For mathematical reasoning type annotation, automatic annotation was verified through manual labeling of 1,000 examples by expert annotators. Results showed 94.1% of examples had exact same set of reasoning types between automatic and human annotations, while 98.79% of individual labels were identical, indicating high accuracy of automatic annotation.
rai:annotationsPerItem: For the newly collected 736 questions, each was independently annotated by three reviewers in the initial annotation phase. For the 1,000 examples used to verify mathematical reasoning categories, expert annotators provided labels from seven candidate categories.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators were graduate students in STEM fields for the new datasets. For human performance baseline evaluation, eligible annotators from Amazon Mechanical Turk had satisfactory annotating history, successfully passed qualification examples, and possessed a high school degree or higher. They had completed more than 5,000 HIT tasks with an acceptance score higher than 0.99.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: EasyOCR was used for OCR text detection. Multimodal Bard was used to generate image captions for augmented LLM experiments. GPT-4 was used as an answer extractor with more than 99.5% accuracy in preliminary study of 200 examples.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is divided into testmini (1,000 examples for model development validation) and test (5,141 examples for standard evaluation). Answer labels for the test set will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination, and an online evaluation platform will be maintained. The authors are committed to maintaining the datasets and refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes questions at different grade levels (elementary school, high school, college, not applicable). Some images contain people, and Multimodal Bard was restricted in responding to images of people. Questions involve celebrities and their profiles (e.g., age gaps between historical figures). The dataset contains 6.57% non-English questions including Chinese and Persian.
rai:dataLimitations: While MathVista encompasses a broad spectrum of tasks and visual contexts, there may be gaps in representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The dataset's focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts, spanning specific domains like science and college-level math, necessitates a more labor-intensive process for collecting high-quality data. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations due to heterogeneity of sources, and annotations lack unified format and structure. The scalability and generalizability to other domains remain a concern. GPT-4V still falls short of human performance by 10.4%, and there is a significant gap between best-performing models and human baseline, indicating room for improvement.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models in visual contexts. It can be used for training, testing, and validation of models. The testmini subset (1,000 examples) is intended for model development validation or for those with limited computing resources. The test set (5,141 examples) is for standard evaluation. The benchmark facilitates development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios and evaluation of LLMs and LMMs capabilities in solving rigorous reasoning tasks. Usage includes assessing models across different tasks (FQA, GPS, MWP, TQA, VQA), mathematical reasoning types (algebraic, arithmetic, geometry, logical, numeric commonsense, scientific, statistical), visual contexts, and grade levels.
